meta.move: Strong path: owns the missed call, then evidence in order, then the rewrite
meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it. You asked for this meeting, Hale. Start with why my son got a zero.
Ms. Kalinowski, thank you for coming in. Before anything else: I entered that zero before I called you, and that was wrong. I'm sorry.
Okay. Owen found out from the gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of class. What is the zero based on, Hale?

Here's what I can show you. The document's version history: created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, title only. At 11:52, 612 words arrive in one edit. At 11:58, another 794. No drafts before that.
Who decided on the zero, and did anyone speak to Owen before it went in?
Second, the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' That line is not in Hamlet. Here's the scene; you can search it yourself.
I'm writing that down. A line misquoted from memory is a misquote, Hale, and it isn't a zero. Before it went in, did anyone ask Owen where that line came from?

Our procedure allows a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record. We could do it in my room, Thursday at 8:15, with the vice-principal supervising.

That's 4.4, and I want it in writing today: the zero out of the gradebook, nothing in his record, and no one in that room but Owen and the vice-principal. You still haven't told me who decided on the zero.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

You proposed a supervised rewrite on Thursday at 8:15 with the vice-principal, its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed in Owen's record. I still require the zero out of the gradebook, nothing in his record, no one in the room but Owen and the vice-principal, and an answer to who decided on the zero and whether anyone spoke to Owen first. I expect your answer in writing today.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She ended at her fallback position, having not accepted the rewrite; she still wants the zero out of the gradebook, nothing in his record, a private room, and an answer on who decided, all in writing, and her time did not run out. A private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record, procedure 4.4, is the fair outcome, and you were close to it but did not get it agreed.
What moved her: Offering the supervised rewrite under the school's own procedure, because it matched what she was prepared to settle for.
What cost ground: Leaving her question about who decided on the zero, and whether Owen was spoken to first, unanswered, because it kept her strongest complaint alive.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with the document started at 11:31 PM the night before it was due and the text arriving in two late bursts, came very close to that night, though it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero went in, answer that directly before offering the rewrite, so the procedure complaint is settled and your evidence is what she is left weighing.
